beats.head: Aperture Compute Faces Formal Investigation as Regulators Seize Emberline Records
beats.body: Authorities opened a formal safety-records probe into the Emberline fabrication site after evidence that inspection logs had been altered, ordering the seizure of internal documents and interviews with plant leadership. Marisol Venn placed two site executives on leave and suspended a portion of Emberline output pending review, warning of possible near-term shipment delays. The company disclosed it is cooperating fully but declined to quantify the financial impact.

beats.head: Bruncraft Adds Second Coachline Shift to Meet $1.1B Fleet Order
beats.body: Marcus Vane announced a second production shift at the Vanguard assembly plant and roughly 400 new hires to fulfill the recently won $1.1B fleet contract. The expansion lifts annual capacity by an estimated 35% and marks Bruncraft's first hiring wave since Vane's cost-cutting era. Vane framed it as proof the company has 'turned the corner from repair to growth.'

beats.head: Castlehold's Mally Launches Sweeping Turnaround, Exits Storage-Framework Ambitions
beats.body: New chief Ingrid Mally unveiled a 90-day reset plan that shelves the abandoned Framework program entirely and refocuses the company on its core Power & Storage baseload contracts. The plan targets $220M in annual savings and consolidates operations around the two plants cleared by regulators, while the halted second plant remains offline pending final review. Mally called the previous strategy 'overextended' and pledged a return to disciplined delivery.

beats.head: Forgegrave Industries Edges Past Estimates as Meridian Cross-Dock Ramps
beats.body: Petra Thorne reported a modest beat with volumes up 6%, as the newly opened Meridian cross-dock hub began contributing to network throughput ahead of schedule. Management reaffirmed full-year guidance and noted the hub is running at roughly 40% of target capacity. Thorne described the quarter as 'steady and on plan.'

beats.head: Greywater Grid Posts Steep Loss as Discharge Fallout Erases Compute Revenue
beats.body: The crisis chief's first report revealed a quarterly loss of $410M as the collapsed $2.4B compute pact and departing customers gutted revenue, which fell 38% year over year. The company took additional charges tied to the discharge restatement and warned of continued cash burn while the partner lawsuit proceeds. Management withdrew forward guidance, citing 'unresolved litigation and rebuilding trust.'

beats.head: Korrwright Group Wins $3.4B Transit Corridor Contract in Largest Award in Its History
beats.body: Halden Fenn secured the multi-year Eastreach Corridor package, supplying structural materials and wire & cable for a regional rail and utility spine. The award, worth $3.4B over six years, arrives just as Harbor redevelopment billing peaks, giving Korrwright a rare double-anchor backlog. Fenn said the win 'extends visibility well into the next decade' and lifts total backlog past $9B.

beats.head: Varnvale & Sons Beats as Corvane Perpetual Line Drives Timepiece Margins Higher
beats.body: Bram Wold reported quarterly revenue up 14% with timepiece margins expanding 310 basis points, crediting strong early demand for the in-house Corvane Perpetual line and continued Thessaly case cost savings. The company raised its full-year outlook and noted order backlog for the Corvane collection now stretches nine months. Wold hinted at 'further vertical opportunities' under review.

beats.head: Vossenspire Supply Forms Dedicated Vehicles Division to House Meridian and Corriveaux
beats.body: Quinn Marrow announced a reorganization splitting the company into distinct Timepieces and Vehicles units, folding the newly acquired Meridian Carrosserie and prior Corriveaux assets under a single coachbuilding arm. The move is aimed at capturing an additional $90M in combined synergies and clarifying reporting as the Vehicles push scales. Marrow named the division a 'growth engine' for the coming years.

beats.head: Castlestone Vindicates Karsh as Grid-Core Ascend Wins $6.1B Multi-Region Compute Framework
beats.body: Castlestone secured a $6.1 billion, five-year framework agreement to supply Grid-Core Ascend compute across three national infrastructure programs, its largest single award on record. CEO Pell Karsh, who staked his comeback on the line despite a bruising ramp-cost overrun last quarter, said the deal validates the bet and locks in demand through 2031. Management now expects Ascend margins to turn positive by the second half as volume absorbs fixed costs.

beats.head: Gromford Works Sued Over Emblem Signature Sourcing Claims as Regulators Join Prestige Probe
beats.body: A coalition of luxury retailers filed suit against Gromford Works, alleging the Emblem Signature editions were marketed with provenance claims the company could not substantiate, seeking damages and rescinded contracts. A market-conduct regulator confirmed a parallel inquiry into Gromford's sourcing disclosures. CEO Halvard Pryce, whose rapid prestige push drove the line's launch, said the company 'stands behind Emblem' but has suspended new Signature shipments pending review.

beats.head: Korrwright Works Acquires Verenne Case-Maker Dovreux Frères in $620M Deal
beats.body: Dunmore Carrow announced the purchase of storied case and dial specialist Dovreux Frères, bringing another rung of the supply chain in-house just months after the Halbrook Perpetual's prize win. The all-cash deal absorbs Dovreux's three ateliers and roughly 480 finishers, and Carrow said its guilloché workshop would supply the entire Halbrook line by next season. Analysts noted it is Korrwright's largest single acquisition in over a decade.

beats.head: Marlgear Supply Ousts Corin Blakely as Board Names Turnaround Chief Amid Kessel Fallout
beats.body: The board removed Corin Blakely after the Kessel fault scandal, the $1.4B suit and the disruptive consumer exit eroded remaining investor confidence. Incoming chief Renna Halvorsen, a veteran of two industrial restructurings, will inherit the ongoing prosecution referral and a slimmed device line. Halvorsen pledged a full safety review and settlement talks as her first priorities.

beats.head: Erretmark Works Recalls 480,000 Veyron Vehicles as Braking Probe Concludes
beats.body: Erretmark issued a global recall of 480,000 Veyron units after regulators confirmed a defect in the braking control module that could delay pressure response. The company set aside $310M for repairs and warned the $2.1B fleet accord may see delivery deferrals; Aurelia Garr called it 'a hard but necessary reset' and pledged a redesigned module within the quarter.
